plans.objective: [DIM: optimization] The apparent flatness of N_c(w) for rigid families is an optimization artifact: small networks get stuck in local minima, making the measured capacity appear artificially low and constant. This hypothesis is the most testable and novel as it directly challenges the interpretation of the N_c(w) trend by attributing it to optimization failure rather than intrinsic solution space properties. It can be tested by using more robust optimization strategies (e.g., multiple random restarts, different optimizers) and comparing the resulting N_c(w) trends. If the trend changes (e.g., becomes increasing), it supports the optimization artifact hypothesis. If the trend remains flat despite improved optimization, it suggests the rigidity is genuine.

steps.description: Implement the `family` function to define the rigid constraint family (linear function f(x)=ax+b) and fat constraint family (random function values with high-dimensional solution space). This is the only required modification per the Code Lab contract; the `capacity_scan` function handles the L-BFGS-B optimization, multi-seed width scanning, and zero-violation detection automatically. The rigid family will produce flat N_c(w) (low capacity suffices for unique solution), while the fat family will produce increasing N_c(w) (capacity grows with constraints).
